title: fix: clarify model catalog schemas
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds explicit community, title, category, alias, and description metadata to OpenAI-compatible model responses.
- Makes the rich catalog’s `community` signal explicit for official and community models.
- Restores valid `video` and `embedding` OpenAPI enums by removing obsolete global alias filtering.
- Documents model-health parameters and response rows, including nullable failure-window latency values.
- Tested with focused Vitest suites, TypeScript, Biome, and the production build.

gist.headline: The catalog labels its jars
gist.blurb: The model shelf got proper labels instead of vibes. OpenAI-compatible listings now carry clearer metadata, and video and embedding entries can appear in the schema without getting lost behind an old filter.
gist.summary: Clarified the model catalog API by adding explicit community, title, category, alias, and description fields to OpenAI-compatible responses, restoring valid video and embedding OpenAPI enums, and documenting nullable model-health latency fields.
gist.impact: Developers can now reliably distinguish official from community models, read richer catalog metadata, discover video and embedding models through valid OpenAPI schemas, and handle model-health response rows correctly.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy model-library garden: neatly labeled seed jars represent official and community models, while a retro terminal shows a clean catalog with video and embedding icons restored to the shelf. Polli acts as the observant librarian, attaching clear labels and checking a small health-status chart; code-plants and flowers make the schema cleanup feel like tending an organized garden.
